functions.name: Pressure Cook / Manual
functions.summary: The catch-all custom pressure-cooking button. You set the time and pressure level yourself.
functions.bestFor: Any recipe that gives a specific time and pressure; the most-used button on the Duo.

functions.name: Soup/Broth
functions.summary: A gentle pressure boil for soups, stocks and bone broth that keeps the liquid clearer.

functions.name: Meat/Stew
functions.summary: Higher, longer pressure to tenderize meat and build hearty stews.
functions.release: Natural release so the meat stays tender
functions.bestFor: Roasts, stew meat, pot roast and large cuts.

functions.name: Bean/Chili
functions.summary: Tuned for dried or soaked beans, legumes and chili.
functions.release: Natural release (beans are foamy and starchy)

functions.name: Poultry
functions.summary: Preset times for chicken and other poultry.
functions.release: Quick for breasts; natural for whole birds
functions.bestFor: Chicken breasts and thighs, whole chicken, turkey pieces.

functions.name: Rice
functions.summary: The only fully automatic program. It senses the water and rice and sets its own time.
functions.bestFor: Regular white rice. Use Multigrain or Manual for brown or wild rice.

functions.name: Multigrain
functions.summary: For tougher whole grains, including an optional warm-water soak on the More setting.
functions.defaultTime: Less 20 / Normal 40 / More 45 min soak + 60 min cook
functions.bestFor: Brown rice, wild rice, barley, mixed and whole grains.

functions.name: Porridge
functions.summary: Creamy grain porridges such as oatmeal and congee.
functions.release: Natural release strongly recommended (starchy and foamy)
functions.bestFor: Oatmeal, congee and creamy grain porridges.

functions.name: Steam
functions.summary: Pressure-steaming on a trivet or basket. Food sits above the water, not in it.
functions.release: Quick release for vegetables to avoid overcooking
functions.bestFor: Vegetables, seafood, eggs, dumplings and reheating.

functions.name: Sauté
functions.summary: Browning, searing, simmering and sautéing with the lid off. No pressure.
functions.levels: Less ~285°F simmer / Normal ~335°F sauté / More ~380°F sear
functions.bestFor: Pre-browning meat and onions, then simmering or thickening sauces after pressure cooking.

functions.name: Slow Cook
functions.summary: Works like a traditional slow cooker. Use a vented or glass lid. No pressure.
functions.release: Not applicable — set the valve to Venting
functions.bestFor: Any recipe written for a traditional slow cooker.

functions.name: Yogurt
functions.summary: Pasteurizes milk (Boil) and incubates it into yogurt. No pressure.
functions.defaultTime: Incubate default 8 h; Boil heats to ~180°F
functions.bestFor: Homemade yogurt and some low-temperature ferments.

functions.name: Keep Warm
functions.summary: Holds finished food at serving temperature. Engages automatically after most cooks.
functions.bestFor: Holding food warm. It does not cook, so don't over-hold delicate dishes.

concepts.title: Natural Release (NPR)
concepts.body: Do nothing when the cook ends — pressure drops on its own over about 10–30 minutes as the pot cools, and food keeps gently cooking. Use it for large meat cuts, soups, broths, beans, grains and porridge, and anything foamy or very full.

concepts.title: Quick Release (QR)
concepts.body: Turn the steam valve to Venting and let the steam jet out; pressure drops in 1–2 minutes. Use it for vegetables, seafood, pasta and eggs that would overcook if left to sit. Keep hands and face clear and use a towel.

concepts.title: Hybrid release
concepts.body: Many recipes say 'Natural 10 min then Quick' — let it release naturally for a set time, then quick-release the rest. It balances tenderness with not overcooking.

concepts.title: Minimum liquid
concepts.body: You need at least 1 cup (about 1.5 cups is safer on the 6-quart) of thin, water-based liquid to build steam. Thick sauces or dairy alone won't reach pressure and can trigger a Burn warning.

concepts.title: Max fill lines
concepts.body: Never fill above the 2/3 PC Max line. For foods that expand or foam — rice, beans, pasta, oats and grains — stay below the 1/2 line.

concepts.title: Come-to-pressure time
concepts.body: The timer doesn't start right away. The pot first heats until it reaches pressure (about 5–15 minutes, longer when cold or full), and only then does the cook countdown begin. Total time = preheat + cook + release.
